source.citation: "Dearborn Street Bridges." Chicagology. The 1834 section transcribing A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, Volume I (the page dates its Andreas text 1886), including the shipwright Nelson R. Norton's own letter.
what_it_does_not_supply: any statement that the bridge was double-leaf
any statement that it was raised by a chain hoist
the deck width, railing, pier or abutment construction
the number or spacing of bents
the height of the gallows frames or of the deck above the water
which bank the draw was hinged on
what_it_supplies: overall length about three hundred feet
draw opening for craft about sixty feet
"gallows pattern" with a frame at either end
the draw lifted (hoisted) rather than swung
built by the shipwright Nelson R. Norton; lumber cut from late 1833, construction begun March 1834
formally accepted by the Trustees in August 1834 per Andreas, correcting Norton's own 1 June
removal ordered July 1839 and the bridge chopped to pieces the next morning
